chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
Regarding the woman who performs Tawaf with the child and performs Sa'i with him, is that sufficient for her and for the child? He said: Yes.

key_terms.تَسْعَى: Sa'i (ritual walking between Safa and Marwah)

ai.seo_question: Does a mother carrying her infant during Hajj rituals fulfill the child's obligation of Tawaf and Sa'i?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ruled that if a woman performs the ritual circumambulation (Tawaf) and the walking between Safa and Marwah (Sa'i) while carrying a young child who has not yet performed these rituals, the child's performance is considered valid and sufficient on their behalf. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of vicarious performance (niyabah) in Hajj rituals, allowing a guardian to fulfill the obligation for a dependent who lacks the physical capacity or independent agency to perform the rites themselves. It underscores the flexibility within the ritual structure to accommodate practical realities of family life during pilgrimage.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the woman who performs Tawaaf with the child, and she performs Sa’ee with it. Would that suffice from her and from the child?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who performs Tawaf with a child and Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah; if this is sufficient for her Tawaf also. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is sufficient.’” (Ahadith 11-13 are best explained in the form of fatwa).
